To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dose-levels associated with first sign of efficacy were higher in phase 1 trials investigating conventional cytotoxin alone as compared to trials investigating molecular targeted agents alone.

first signs of efficacy were observed in a similar proportion of all trials, but were less frequently observed at lower doses in trials investigating molecular target agents, and that maximum tolerated dose was more frequently established in trials of conventional cytotoxins than in trials of molecular targeted agents.

1) the MTD is more frequently observed in trials investigating conventional cytotoxin and 2) first sign of efficacy is more frequently observed at the early dose level for conventional cytotoxins as compared to MTA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dose escalation process of phase 1 trials in contemporary oncology.
the question of whether or not the first dose level of a new agent is likely to be efficacious.
the dose levels at which clinical benefit was first observed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the first sign of efficacy is more likely to be observed in the first three dose levels in trials with conventional cytotoxic agents, while MTD is more likely to occur at a higher dose level in trials with molecular targeted agents.
MTD is less frequently reached in MTA trials and that the first sign of efficacy is observed later in the dose escalation schedule than with cytotoxic agents.
dose seeking trials with MTA are less efficient than those with cytotoxic agents in terms of both dose escalation and clinical efficacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dose escalation in phase 1 trials investigating MTA should not be stopped as soon as a sign of efficacy is observed.
MTD is reached at the fifth dose-level and first sign of efficacy is observed at the first four dose-levels in the majority of the phase 1 trials.
MTA could be more efficacious at low doses than cytotoxic drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dose levels are not always a good indicator of clinical activity.
dose seeking phase 2 trials should be performed to establish optimal dose of MTA.
dose-escalation should not be stopped as early as possible in MTA trials.
